standard_prerequisites.name: Sheaf theoretically empty objects and the empty topos
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the notion of a nonempty object used to reduce the converse direction to a single test object.

core_obligations: Show that generators x_1, ..., x_r of M define global sections generating the constant sheaf, giving one direction of (1) (proof lines 8576-8580).

Conversely, given a non-sheaf-theoretically-empty object U, refine a covering and a finite generating family so that the sections come from elements x_{ij} of M, which then define global sections generating the restriction to U (proof lines 8581-8592).

Show that elements whose global sections generate the constant sheaf must generate M: refine a covering so that the coefficients lie in the ring itself, and use that some covering member contains a nonempty object to conclude (proof lines 8593-8620).
Deduce statement (2) about finite presentation from the same two-sided analysis.
proof_roadmap: Prove both directions of the finite type statement by refining coverings.
Use a non-sheaf-theoretically-empty object to reduce to a single test object.
Transfer the argument to finite presentation.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes finite type and finite presentability of the constant sheaf associated to a module in terms of the module itself, assuming the topos is not empty. The proof of the finite type statement is two-sided: global sections of the constant sheaf coming from generators of the module generate it, and conversely a finite local generating family may be refined so that its sections come from elements of the module, which then generate; the second half additionally shows that elements whose global sections generate must generate the module, by refining a covering and using that a non-sheaf-theoretically-empty object has at least one covering member contributing (proof lines 8576-8620). H2: the two covering refinements and the reduction to a single nonempty object are the substance, and both are written out.
